raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

The scheduler ends some requests outside the output stream:

- aborted while queued (`/abort_request`, `SGLANG_REQ_WAITING_TIMEOUT`);
- evicted or rejected by priority scheduling (`--max-queued-requests`, priority disabled);
- aborted on retraction when the KV pool is full;
- aborted while chunked, or in the PD decode retracted queue.

It reports each one as an `AbortReq` on the ZMQ tokenizer socket, and Python's `TokenizerManager` turns that into the request's final frame (`_handle_abort_req`). In Rust mode nothing reads that socket, so these clients never got a terminal frame: a stream hung until the client gave up, and a unary request never received its status.

## Modifications

- `python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py`: the nine abort sites now go through a new `Scheduler.send_abort_output`, the counterpart of `send_control_output`. With a Rust server it calls `rust_server.push_abort`; otherwise it sends the `AbortReq` to the tokenizer socket as before. Python mode is unchanged.
- `python/sglang/srt/rust_server/server.py`: `RustServer.push_abort` pushes a one-request terminal batch to the Rust egress with the abort finish reason (the scheduler's, or Python's `"Abort in waiting queue"` default) and no new tokens. The Rust frontend renders it like any abort finish: a final stream frame, or the finish's status code for a unary request, as Python does. The batch carries the request's own prompt, cached and reasoning token counts, so it does not reset what the stream already reported.
- Tests: `test_rust_server_extension.py` gains `test_scheduler_aborts_reach_the_rust_egress` (in Rust mode the abort becomes the one-row batch with the request's counts; without the Rust server it still goes to the tokenizer socket). Scheduler unit tests that build a scheduler with `Scheduler.__new__` or a `SimpleNamespace` now set `rust_server = None`, which every real scheduler sets in `maybe_init_rust_server`, or fake `send_abort_output` directly (`test_weight_versions.py`).

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: no model or numerics change.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable: the abort path only; the per-token output path is untouched.

## Test plan

- `pytest test/registered/unit/multimodal/rust/shared/test_rust_server_extension.py test/registered/unit/utils/test_weight_versions.py test/registered/unit/dllm/test_gemma4_uniform_lifecycle.py test/registered/unit/managers/test_multimodal_abort_cleanup.py test/registered/unit/managers/test_priority_scheduling_disaggregation.py test/registered/unit/managers/test_scheduler_chunked_abort_race.py test/registered/unit/managers/test_scheduler_pause_generation.py test/registered/unit/managers/test_scheduler_timeouts.py` on CPU: 134 passed, 47 subtests passed.
- Swept `test/` for every other test that sets `ipc_channels` on a scheduler fixture (`test_scheduler_flush_cache.py`, `test_scheduler_health_check_signal.py`): both already set `rust_server`, so no other fixture reaches `send_abort_output` without it.
- `pre-commit run --files <changed files>`: all hooks passed.
- `rust/`: unchanged; the Rust side already renders an abort finish reason from a decode result batch.
- Not run here: a live Rust-mode server. A manual check would start a Rust-mode and a Python-mode server with `--max-running-requests 1` and `SGLANG_REQ_WAITING_TIMEOUT=3`, hold the slot with a long stream, and confirm that a unary request queued behind it gets a 503 and a streaming request cancelled with `/abort_request` ends with an abort `finish_reason` and `[DONE]` in both modes.

- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
